title: Proportional Reasoning–1: Ratios and Proportions
seo_title: Proportional Reasoning–1 Class 8 Worksheet with Answers (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 8, Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 7: Proportional Reasoning–1
standard_text: Ratios, equivalent ratios, proportion, the unitary method and sharing in a given ratio (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 8)
meta_desc: Class 8 Proportional Reasoning–1 worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 7): ratios, simplest form, equivalent ratios, proportions, unitary method and sharing. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: a : b = c : d means a × d = b × c
key_sub: Multiply or divide both parts of a ratio by the same number.
body_html:
How it works

A ratio a : b compares two quantities by division. Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both parts by the same number: 6 : 4 = 3 : 2.

Four numbers are in proportion if a : b = c : d, that is a × d = b × c.

Unitary method: find the value of one, then multiply. To share in the ratio 2 : 3, split into 5 equal parts.

Example

Share ₹450 in the ratio 4 : 5.

9 parts: 1 part = ₹50

Answer: ₹200 and ₹250

Example

Find x if 3 : 8 = 12 : x.

3 × 4 = 12, so 8 × 4

Answer: 32

Common mistakes

  • Adding the same number to both parts instead of multiplying (additive thinking).
  • Writing the ratio in the wrong order.
  • Dividing by one part instead of the total number of parts when sharing.

items.q: Are 2, 5, 6 and 15 in proportion (2 : 5 = 6 : 15)?
c: Only if all four are even
items.e: 2 × 15 = 30 and 5 × 6 = 30: products of extremes and means are equal, so Yes.

items.q: Are 3, 8, 18 and 48 in proportion (3 : 8 = 18 : 48)?
c: Only if all four are even
items.e: 3 × 48 = 144 and 8 × 18 = 144: products of extremes and means are equal, so Yes.
